PAGE TITLE: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS FORWARD LOOKING
2025 and Beyond

KEY FACTS:
- NASA continues to plan for the future of deep space exploration, preparing for the launch of Artemis II and Artemis III.
- Artemis II will mark NASA’s first crewed mission of the Orion spacecraft, following Artemis I which demonstrated the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
- Four Commercial Crew missions and ninety experiments are expected to be conducted using commercial facilities on ISS over the next two fiscal years.
- NASA is launching the Total and Spectral Solar Irradiance Sensor 2 mission, completing the Operational Readiness Review of the NASA-Indian Space Research Organisation Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission, and completing the Landsat Next System Requirements Review and GRACE-C Critical Design Review by the end of FY 2025.
- Europa Clipper, a mission headed for Jupiter’s moon Europa, is among projects slated to better understand the solar system and the universe beyond.
- The Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx) is targeted for launch in FY 2025 to provide the first all-sky spectral survey of hundreds of millions of galaxies.
- SMD projects in development include the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, the Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP), the Dragonfly mission, Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor, and the Multi-Slit Solar Explorer (MUSE).
- By the end of FY 2025, NASA will demonstrate leadership in space technology by enhancing partnerships with industry through initializing several tipping point opportunities.
